summary: Defines procedures and messages for providing BGP-based services over Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6), including Layer 3 VPN, Ethernet VPN, and Internet services. It builds on BGP/MPLS IP VPNs (RFC 4364) and BGP MPLS-Based Ethernet VPN (RFC 7432), replacing MPLS labels with SRv6 mechanisms. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines how BGP can advertise service routes that use SRv6 instead of MPLS labels. The receiving edge router uses the advertised IPv6 service identifier to send traffic to the correct service at the far end.

subtitle: Signals BGP service identifiers for L3VPN, EVPN and Internet services over an SRv6 core.

tldr.problem: BGP VPN services traditionally signal MPLS labels, while an SRv6 network needs IPv6-based service identifiers.
tldr.mechanism: The egress PE advertises an SRv6 Service SID in new BGP Prefix-SID TLVs; the ingress PE uses the SID as the destination of an outer IPv6 packet.
tldr.outcome: The procedures cover Layer 3 VPN, Ethernet VPN and Internet services. RFC 9819 later updates this RFC.

today: RFC 9252 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 9819.

sections.title: BGP Services over an SRv6 Core
sections.content:
Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) uses IPv6 for the data plane. BGP advertises service prefixes from an egress Provider Edge (PE) to ingress PEs. This RFC defines procedures for Layer 3 VPN, Ethernet VPN and Internet services.

The egress PE advertises an SRv6 Service SID with the service route. The ingress PE places that SID in the destination field of an outer IPv6 header. For best-effort service, the underlay needs plain IPv6 forwarding.
sections.plainLanguage: The far-end PE advertises an IPv6 address that identifies the service. The ingress PE sends customer traffic to that address inside an outer IPv6 packet.

sections.title: SRv6 Service TLVs
sections.content:
The RFC adds two TLVs to the BGP Prefix-SID attribute: type 5 for Layer 3 services and type 6 for Layer 2 services. Each includes a length, a reserved field and a list of service sub-TLVs. The reserved field is set to zero by the sender.

The SRv6 SID Information sub-TLV carries a 16-octet SID, flags, an endpoint behavior value and optional data sub-sub-TLVs. A receiver should use the first SID Information sub-TLV when several are present. Unknown endpoint behaviors are not automatically invalid.
sections.plainLanguage: The BGP update labels whether the service is Layer 2 or Layer 3. A nested field carries the IPv6 service identifier and its endpoint behavior.

sections.title: Transposing Part of a Service SID
sections.content:
The SID Structure sub-sub-TLV describes the bit lengths of the locator block, locator node, function and argument. It also records a transposition offset and length. These fields tell the receiver how to reconstruct a SID when part of it is carried elsewhere.

For efficient BGP updates, a common part of a SID can remain in the service TLV while a variable part is carried in an existing MPLS label field. The label field can hold 20 bits in some service encodings and 24 bits in EVPN encodings. The bits moved out of the SID value are set to zero there.
sections.plainLanguage: Some service routes can store a varying part of the SID in an existing label field. The receiver uses the structure fields to put the pieces back together.

sections.title: Layer 3 VPN and Internet Services
sections.content:
For Layer 3 services, the egress PE advertises a Service SID in the Layer 3 Service TLV. The ingress PE checks that the SID is reachable before using the route in best-path selection. The SID may identify a table lookup or a cross-connect at the egress PE.

For VPN routes, the existing label field may carry a transposed part of the SID; otherwise it is set to Implicit NULL. The RFC covers IPv4 VPN, IPv6 VPN, global IPv4 and global IPv6 service routes.
sections.plainLanguage: The ingress PE checks that it can reach the advertised service identifier before selecting the route. The identifier tells the egress PE how to handle the packet for that service.

sections.title: Ethernet VPN Routes
sections.content:
EVPN route types 1, 2, 3 and 5 can carry SRv6 Service SIDs. The ingress PE encapsulates the customer Ethernet frame in an outer IPv6 packet and uses the service SID associated with the route.

Different route types use Layer 2 or Layer 3 service TLVs and may place part of the SID in an existing label field. Route type 4 and route types 6, 7 and 8 do not carry these service TLVs under this RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: Several EVPN route types carry a service identifier for Ethernet traffic. Other route types keep their existing processing and do not include these TLVs.

sections.title: Malformed Updates and Security
sections.content:
A malformed Service TLV causes the BGP treat-as-withdraw action. An unknown type is not itself malformed. If no valid SRv6 SID information remains, the route is ineligible during best-path selection.

The RFC relies on the security of BGP sessions and the SRv6 domain. It warns that filtering errors could expose service SIDs to unauthorized peers and points operators to SRv6 access-control guidance. The unit metadata lists RFC 9819 as an update.
sections.plainLanguage: If the service information is malformed, the router treats the route as withdrawn. Operators also need to filter BGP information and protect access to SRv6 addresses.

fields.name: TLV Type
fields.desc: 5 for L3 Service or 6 for L2 Service.

fields.name: TLV Length
fields.desc: Length of the TLV value in octets.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Sender sets to zero; receiver ignores it.

fields.name: Transposition Length
fields.desc: Number of SID bits carried in the label field.

fields.name: Transposition Offset
fields.desc: Starting bit position in the SID.
